mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in at least 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day forward returns in more than 50% of such co-occurring events.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL) above 0.6% signals accelerating inflation, prompting expectations of tighter monetary policy, which in turn reduces equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 0.6% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month and a fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.3 percentage points signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 0.5% AND UNRATE < previous month - 0.3pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of such co-occurring events.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 2% signals a shift from consumption to saving, which typically precedes a pullback in consumer spending and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 8% from the previous year's average, combined with a concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1%, signals broad-based weakness in the housing and manufacturing sectors, which reduces GDP growth and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous year average - 8% AND INDPRO < previous year average - 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of such co-occurring events.
